title.narrative: EU Support to Migration Management in Serbia - Access to Health Services II

description.narrative: This Action aims to respond to the resilience needs of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers in Serbia, through support to the national health authorities. Adequate and accessible health care services in all centres at the primary, secondary and tertiary health care levels will be supported in order to effectively respond to the needs of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers in Serbia.

description.narrative: All refugees, migrants and asylum seekers who are in the territory of the Republic of Serbia have access to health care at all three levels primary, secondary and tertiary.If any of the migrant population is in reception centers or asylum centers, health services at the primary level are provided to them in the clinic of the reception center by the engaged medical team. If the clinic is not equipped with the necessary medical equipment, the medical teams refer them to the local health center for analysis.If the patient needs further diagnostics that require laboratory tests or services for which it is necessary to use specific medical equipment, migrants, refugees and asylum seekers are referred further to the competent health center. If there are medical indications that go beyond the primary level of services, migrants, refugees and asylum seekers are further referred to secondary and tertiary level institutions. title.narrative: Output 1.3 Satisfactory sanitary and hygienic conditions are provided in the migrant accommodation centresr relevant partnersa

description.narrative: Due to increased hygienic and epidemiological risks, territorially competent institutes for public health conduct hygienic and epidemiological surveillance in all centres for accommodation of the migrant population with water and food sampling with obligatory services of disinfection, disinsection, deratisation and depediculation. In migrant transit and asylum centres, where cases of body lice infestation and cases of scabies have been registered, measures and activities have been continuously conducted in order to suppress body lice infestation and to prevent the emergence of new cases of infestation in the migrant population, including daily reporting on the registered number of infected persons and depediculation measures undertaken.In accordance with epidemiological indications and the proposed measures for prevention and control of infectious diseases, institutes for public health provide DDD services. However, the Belgrade City Institute for Public Health and the Subotica Institute for Public Health have no jurisdiction to provide DDD services. Accordingly, in Obrenovac and Krnjaa, hygienic and epidemiological surveillance is carried out by the City Institute for Public Health in Belgrade, while DDD services are carried out by the Institute for Biocides and Medical Ecology. In RC Subotica, hygienic and epidemiological surveillance is carried out by IPH Subodica, while DDD services are carried out by the Institute for Public Health Sombor. In the remaining centres, all other territorially competent institutes for public health also provide hygienic epidemiological surveillance and DDD services.In conditions of collective accommodation with temporary characteristics (including accommodation for migrants), due to increased hygienicepidemiological risks, the competent institute or public health institution was implementing the following activities: At least four times per month, sanitary and hygienic surveillance of accommodation facilities, which included (from the moment of the current epidemiological situation, hygienic and epidemiological supervision is carried out once a week, i.e. 45 times a month): control of maintenance conditions, as well as maintenance of general and personal hygiene; control of the supply of safe drinking water; control of the removal of all types of waste materials and other environmental factors can have an impact on health; controlling the presence of potential sources of pollution of water, food and the environment; This control also includes the sampling and testing of the health safety of food and drinking water.Disinfection of the premises, Deratisation, Disinsection After the services are carried out, the institutes for public health collect reports on the conducted hygienic and epidemiological supervisions, reports on water and food testing, certificates on the performed DDD services, based on which they prepare an invoice and specification of costs. After submitting the necessary documentation and verification by the PIU, the payment procedure is initiated.

title.narrative: Output 1.1. Ensure adequate access to all types of necessary healthcare services for migrants, refugees and asylum seekersthened

description.narrative: Migrants, refugees and asylum seekers have access to all types of health services at all three levels of health care. Previous emergency situations have shown that certain conditions/syndromes should be considered as priorities and monitored systematically. Cases are reported according to the case definitions defined for this purpose. For other diseases/conditions (e.g. WNV, scabies, pediculosis etc.) cases are reported according to the case definitions which are using for case detection in the general population. Based on the experience from the field other include mainly non communicable diseases/conditions that are most frequent worldwide such as: high blood pressure, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes etc.Considering that most of the migrants are staying illegally in the territory of the Republic of Serbia (they do not have a granted asylum status) there is no possibility for full implementation of the provisions of the Health Care Law (Official Gazette of RS, no. 25/2019), and the Health Insurance Law ( Official Gazette of RS, no. 25/2019 and 92/2023), which is why it is not legally possible to provide health care services to migrants as foreseen by the contractual obligations of the Republic Fund for Health Insurance towards health institutions. For insured persons in RS, the Republic Fund for Health Insurance shall cover the costs of provided health care services based on the Rule Book on the prices of services classified into several categories in accordance with the International classification 10. However, in addition to the costs of services, the Republic Fund for Health Insurance shall perform regular transfer of wages for healthcare workers, expendable material, energy resources, and maintenance of medical equipment, medical material and medicaments. Shortages in funds for these services and fixed expenses shall be compensated by the Republic Fund for Health Insurance through regular transfer from the budget of RS. We also point out that part of the funds, the expendable material, and other medical necessities cannot be used according to the law for the needs of uninsured persons, which is why direct transfers from the budget of the Ministry of Health are used as an instrument for compensation of health care costs of migrants. Taking into consideration that in the health care of migrants and with absolute accessibility of health care provided to them, it is not possible to use the methodology and resources of the Republic Fund for Health Insurance. When determining the amount of compensated costs, the Ministry of health had applied the methodology on the basis of which all health care services were reduced to the most frequent categories of reviews and services required for migrants.Vaccination is carried out in local health centers according to the vaccination plan of the local population. The plan is to vaccinate against measles, mumps, rubella, polio, diphtheria, tetanus and hepatitis B. nd legislative processes. It contributed to addressing gender, inclusiveness, and minority rights in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Sindh Provincial Assemblies.The progress made in these areas collectively contributed to the enhanced legislative, oversight, budgetary, and representation capacity, promoting effective governance, transparency, accountability, inclusivity, gender equality, and human rights in the legislative process.

description.narrative: The general impact of the Action was to enable the migrant population to have access to all health services, as well as to provide funds and mechanisms of the Ministry of Health for the construction and improvement of the migration management system in Serbia in accordance with the requirements of the European integration process.Healthcare institutions in Serbia at all levels provide healthcare for all refugees, migrants and asylum seekers in the same way as for citizens of Serbia, but the healthcare system of Serbia faces a lack of human and material resources to adequately cover the needs of the migrant population. In particular, this project contributed to: a significant professional workforce that could be recruited as needed; experienced personnel in the administration of beneficiaries capable of programming and implementing EUfunded projects; a better adapted migrationoriented system for the provision of health services with a special focus on vulnerable groups and increasing their resilience; systems/mechanisms for coordination and exchange of information at the national level.The Ministry of Health performs the activities of the state administration which refers to the following: organisation of health care, system of compulsory health care insurance, realisation of projects financed from the preaccession funds of the European Union, donations and other forms of development assistance, monitoring of health status and assessment of health needs of the population, health and sanitary surveillance. The activity in the field of public health in Serbia is performed by the Institute of Public Health of Serbia Dr Milan Jovanovi Batut (IPHS), together with the network of 24 institutes of public health. Public health care in Serbia is provided according to the Decree on the Plan of the stateowned health care network institution:Primary level: 160 primary health centres, Secondary level: 74 health institutions: 40 general hospitals, of which 34 specialist hospitals including 18 special rehabilitation hospitals; Tertiary level: 30 health institutions, 4 clinic centres, 6 clinic hospital centres, 7 clinics and 13 institutes;Multiple levels: 34 health institutions of which 24 institutes for public health In case of need for special types of health care, all health institutions and resources of the health system are available to the migrant population at all times, in accordance with the above organisational scheme.

description.narrative: The general impact of the Action was to enable the migrant population to have access to all health services, as well as to provide funds and mechanisms of the Ministry of Health for the construction and improvement of the migration management system in Serbia in accordance with the requirements of the European integration process.Healthcare institutions in Serbia at all levels provide healthcare for all refugees, migrants and asylum seekers in the same way as for citizens of Serbia, but the healthcare system of Serbia faces a lack of human and material resources to adequately cover the needs of the migrant population. In particular, this project contributed to: a significant professional workforce that could be recruited as needed; experienced personnel in the administration of beneficiaries capable of programming and implementing EUfunded projects; a better adapted migrationoriented system for the provision of health services with a special focus on vulnerable groups and increasing their resilience; systems/mechanisms for coordination and exchange of information at the national level.The Ministry of Health performs the activities of the state administration which refers to the following: organisation of health care, system of compulsory health care insurance, realisation of projects financed from the preaccession funds of the European Union, donations and other forms of development assistance, monitoring of health status and assessment of health needs of the population, health and sanitary surveillance. The activity in the field of public health in Serbia is performed by the Institute of Public Health of Serbia Dr Milan Jovanovi Batut (IPHS), together with the network of 24 institutes of public health. Public health care in Serbia is provided according to the Decree on the Plan of the stateowned health care network institution:Primary level: 160 primary health centres, Secondary level: 74 health institutions: 40 general hospitals, of which 34 specialist hospitals including 18 special rehabilitation hospitals; Tertiary level: 30 health institutions, 4 clinic centres, 6 clinic hospital centres, 7 clinics and 13 institutes;Multiple levels: 34 health institutions of which 24 institutes for public health In case of need for special types of health care, all health institutions and resources of the health system are available to the migrant population at all times, in accordance with the above organisational scheme.
